items.stem: Logan's speech best illustrates which of the following?
items.stimulus:
Questions 13–16 refer to the following excerpt.

"I appeal to any white man to say if ever he entered Logan's cabin hungry and he gave him not meat... During the course of the last long and bloody war Logan remained idle in his cabin, an advocate for peace... I had even thought to have lived with you but for the injuries of one man. Colonel Cresap, the last spring, in cold blood and unprovoked, murdered all the relations of Logan... There runs not a drop of my blood in the veins of any living creature. This called on me for revenge. I have sought it. I have killed many... But do not harbor a thought that mine is the joy of fear. Logan never felt fear."
—Logan (Tah-gah-jute), speech recorded 1774 (abridged)
options: A. Native leaders uniformly rejected all diplomacy and negotiation with colonists
B. British officials successfully mediated frontier disputes between settlers and tribes
C. Cycles of personal revenge and retaliatory violence shaped frontier relations
D. The Proclamation of 1763 permanently ended all frontier violence
items.explanation: Logan describes a personal cycle: his friendship with whites, Cresap's murder of his family, and his revenge killings — illustrating how frontier violence escalated through retaliation.

Questions 37–40 refer to the following excerpt.

"I come to present the strong claims of suffering humanity. I come as the advocate of helpless, forgotten, insane, and idiotic men and women... I proceed, gentlemen, briefly to call your attention to the present state of insane persons confined within this Commonwealth, in cages, closets, cellars, stalls, pens! Chained, naked, beaten with rods, and lashed into obedience."
—Dorothea Dix, Memorial to the Legislature of Massachusetts, 1843 (abridged)
options: A. Founding the American Red Cross after the war
B. Leading Union Army nurses as superintendent during the Civil War
C. Writing the antislavery novel Uncle Tom's Cabin
D. Leading the Seneca Falls women's rights convention of 1848
items.explanation: During the Civil War, Dix organized and led the Union's corps of army nurses — the most prominent woman in federal service of the war.

items.stem: Long's 'Share Our Wealth' program was primarily a response to
items.stimulus:
Questions 41–44 refer to the following excerpt.

Senator Huey Long charged that a tiny elite hoarded the nation's wealth while millions suffered in the Depression. He proposed capping personal fortunes, guaranteeing every family a homestead and a minimum annual income, shortening the workweek, and providing free college and old-age pensions — all funded by steep taxes on the rich.
—After Huey P. Long, 'Share Our Wealth' radio address, February 1934 (paraphrased)
options: A. The Cold War and superpower rivalry with the Soviets
B. The Great Depression and discontent with early New Deal relief
C. Reconstruction and its constitutional amendments
D. The Panic of 1893 and the depression of the 1890s
items.explanation: Long launched Share Our Wealth in 1934 as Depression suffering persisted, charging that Roosevelt's New Deal did too little for ordinary people.

items.stem: Bradford's account of Squanto illustrates
items.stimulus:
Questions 45–48 refer to the following excerpt.

"Squanto... was a special instrument sent of God for their good beyond their expectation. He directed them how to set their corn, where to take fish, and to procure other commodities, and was also their pilot to bring them to unknown places for their profit, and never left them till he died."
—William Bradford, Of Plymouth Plantation (abridged)
options: A. The complete absence of Native-colonist contact
B. The total military dominance of the Pilgrims
C. The critical role of Native aid in colonial survival
D. Spanish missionary influence in New England
items.explanation: Bradford credits Squanto with teaching the Pilgrims to plant corn, fish, and navigate — aid without which the colony might not have survived.

items.stem: Bradford's description of Squanto as 'a special instrument sent of God' reflects

options: A. Enlightenment rationalism and confidence in human reason

items.stem: The Pilgrims' survival at Plymouth depended most directly on

items.stem: Bradford's history is best characterized as
items.stimulus:

items.stem: The poster's imagery was designed primarily to
items.stimulus:
Questions 49–52 refer to the following poster.

[An 1890s Buffalo Bill's Wild West show poster depicts cowboys, Native American performers, and sharpshooters on horseback circling a stagecoach, beneath the banner 'Buffalo Bill's Wild West — Congress of Rough Riders of the World.']
options: A. Document actual frontier life with strict accuracy
B. Romanticize the West for eastern and European audiences
C. Recruit soldiers to fight in the Indian Wars
D. Promote investment in railroad bonds
items.explanation: The Wild West show was entertainment that packaged a romanticized frontier — cowboys, 'Indians,' sharpshooters — for paying audiences in the East and Europe.

items.stem: The Wild West show's portrayal of Native Americans
items.stimulus:
Questions 49–52 refer to the following poster.

[An 1890s Buffalo Bill's Wild West show poster depicts cowboys, Native American performers, and sharpshooters on horseback circling a stagecoach, beneath the banner 'Buffalo Bill's Wild West — Congress of Rough Riders of the World.']
options: A. Accurately represented tribal cultures and traditions
B. Presented stereotyped performances that shaped myths of the West
C. Opposed federal Indian policy and reservation confinement
D. Brought an end to the reservation system entirely
items.explanation: The shows staged 'Indian attacks' and battle reenactments that fixed stereotypes of Native Americans as savage foes in the popular imagination.

items.stem: The popularity of such shows in the 1890s reflected

[An 1890s Buffalo Bill's Wild West show poster depicts cowboys, Native American performers, and sharpshooters on horseback circling a stagecoach, beneath the banner 'Buffalo Bill's Wild West — Congress of Rough Riders of the World.']
options: A. Widespread opposition to immigration

items.explanation: As the census declared the frontier closed (1890) and America industrialized, audiences romanticized a West that was already disappearing.

items.stem: A historian using this poster as evidence would most appropriately use it to study
items.stimulus:
Questions 49–52 refer to the following poster.

[An 1890s Buffalo Bill's Wild West show poster depicts cowboys, Native American performers, and sharpshooters on horseback circling a stagecoach, beneath the banner 'Buffalo Bill's Wild West — Congress of Rough Riders of the World.']
options: A. The engineering of western railroads
